jaipur.description: Known as the Pink City, Jaipur is a vibrant destination filled with historic forts, magnificent palaces, and colorful bazaars.

overview.tips: Hire local government-approved guides at forts. Try Pyaz Kachori at Rawat Misthan Bhandar. Bargain at Bazaars.

hotels.name: Umaid Bhawan Heritage Hotel
hotels.highlight: Heritage-style architecture, rooftop restaurant with traditional dance, clean pool.

hotels.name: Pearl Palace Heritage
hotels.highlight: Highly-rated boutique heritage hotel with unique, artist-designed rooms.

hotels.name: The Oberoi Rajvilas
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury traditional fort setting, private pools, 5-star spa, royal service.

spots.name: Amber Palace (Amer Fort)
spots.highlight: Stunning yellow-sandstone fort, Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), elephant/jeep rides.

spots.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
spots.highlight: Honeycomb pink facade with 953 tiny windows designed for royal ladies.

spots.name: City Palace
spots.highlight: Living royal residence featuring museums, weapon galleries, and peacocks.

spots.name: Jantar Mantar
spots.highlight: UNESCO World Heritage site with the world's largest stone sundial.

spots.name: Johari Bazaar & Bapu Bazaar
spots.highlight: Traditional jewelry, silver, block-printed fabrics, and authentic mojari shoes.

schedule.activity: Visit early to catch the morning sunlight shining through the facade. Photograph from across the street at Wind View Cafe.
Explore the royal courtyards, Peacock Gate, and see the giant instruments of Jantar Mantar right next door.
Wander through the pink-tinted bazaars, shop for local handicrafts, textiles, and grab snacks like Golgappa.
Arrive early to avoid queues. Explore the massive gateways, the Diwan-i-Aam, and the breathtaking Mirror Palace.
Visit the beautiful, symmetric 16th-century stepwell nearby. Great for photography.
Drive up the Aravalli hills to Nahargarh Fort. Watch the sun set over the entire city of Jaipur from Padao Restaurant.
Marvel at the Indo-Saracenic architecture. See the ancient artifacts, paintings, and an Egyptian mummy.
A historic temple complex set within a mountain pass. Known for natural springs and hundreds of friendly monkeys.
Experience Rajasthani culture. Enjoy folk dances, camel rides, puppet shows, and a massive authentic Rajasthani thali dinner.

tokyo.description: Tokyo is a dynamic neon metropolis blending ultramodern technology, pop culture, and centuries-old shinto shrines and quiet gardens.

overview.tips: Get a digital Suica card on Apple Wallet or Google Pay. Trains stop running around midnight. Tipping is not practiced.

hotels.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
hotels.highlight: The famous Godzilla Hotel, located in the heart of Shinjuku's nightlife area.

hotels.name: APA Hotel & Resort Nishishinjuku
hotels.highlight: Great value, features a rooftop pool and a large public hot bath.

hotels.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
hotels.highlight: Iconic luxury hotel made famous by the movie 'Lost in Translation'.

spots.name: Shibuya Crossing
spots.highlight: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing. View it from high above at Shibuya Sky.

spots.name: Senso-ji Temple
spots.highlight: Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in Asakusa.

spots.name: teamLab Planets
spots.highlight: Digital art museum where you walk through water and immersive light exhibits.

spots.name: Akihabara Electric Town
spots.highlight: Mecca for anime, manga, gaming, electronics, and themed cafes.

spots.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
spots.highlight: A serene forest shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji in the center of Tokyo.

schedule.activity: Walk through the Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and shop for traditional souvenirs and snacks along Nakamise Street.
Grab lunch at a themed cafe, explore multi-story arcade centers, and search for anime collectibles.
Ascend the tallest structure in Japan for sunset. Enjoy panoramic views of the city stretching to Mt. Fuji.
Walk under the massive torii gates into the peaceful forest. Afterward, check out eccentric fashion on Takeshita Street.
Cross the famous Shibuya crossing, take a photo with the Hachiko statue, and head up to Shibuya Sky for 360-degree open-air views.
Have dinner in Shinjuku. Explore the atmospheric alleyways of Omoide Yokocho ('Memory Lane') for grilled yakitori and beers.
Try fresh sea urchin, wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki (sweet omelet), and strawberry daifuku from traditional stalls.
Immerse yourself in infinite crystal universes, floating orchid gardens, and walk barefoot through warm water.
See the Giant Gundam statue, take pictures at the replica Statue of Liberty, and walk along the beach to watch the Rainbow Bridge light up.

paris.description: The City of Light, Paris is an international center for fashion, gastronomy, world-famous art museums, and stunning architecture along the Seine.

overview.tips: Book Louvre tickets weeks in advance. Say 'Bonjour' when entering shops. The metro is faster than taxis in heavy traffic.

hotels.name: Hotel Caron de Beaumarchais
hotels.highlight: Boutique hotel with 18th-century Parisian style, close to historic cafes.

hotels.name: Generator Paris Hostel
hotels.highlight: Affordable chic design hostel, rooftop bar overlooking Montmartre.

hotels.name: Hotel Plaza Athénée
hotels.highlight: Classic French palace luxury, red awnings, views of the Eiffel Tower.

spots.name: Eiffel Tower
spots.highlight: The symbol of Paris. Look for the twinkling light show every hour at night.

spots.name: Louvre Museum
spots.highlight: The world's largest art museum, home to the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.

spots.name: Sacré-Cœur & Montmartre
spots.highlight: Charming artist hilltop village with panoramic views of Paris.

spots.name: Palace of Versailles
spots.highlight: Opulent royal palace featuring the Hall of Mirrors and vast gardens.

spots.name: Seine River Cruise
spots.highlight: A relaxing 1-hour cruise passing Notre Dame, Louvre, and historical bridges.

schedule.activity: Enter through the glass pyramid. Prioritize the Denon wing to see the Mona Lisa, Winged Victory, and Liberty Leading the People.

schedule.spot: Tuileries Garden & Place de la Concorde
schedule.activity: Grab a baguette sandwich, sit in the famous green chairs, and walk down the Champs-Élysées to the Arc de Triomphe.
schedule.transport: Metro Line 1 to Charles de Gaulle

schedule.activity: Watch the sunset from Trocadéro Gardens, then board an evening cruise to see Paris light up.
Climb up to the white basilica on the hill. Wander down the cobblestone streets of Place du Tertre to see local painters.
Admire the Gothic facade of Notre-Dame, explore nearby Shakespeare and Company bookstore, and have a coffee in Saint-Germain-des-Prés.
Explore the largest collection of Impressionist masterpieces (Monet, Van Gogh, Renoir) inside a gorgeous old railway station.
Take a half-day trip to Versailles. Tour the magnificent apartments, Hall of Mirrors, and hire a bike to explore the royal gardens.
Return to Paris and walk through the historic Jewish quarter. Try the world-famous falafel at L'As du Fallafel, and shop in boutique stores.
Conclude your trip in a traditional wine cave. Sample flight of Bordeaux wines paired with aged Comte and Brie cheeses.

new york.description: Known as the Big Apple, New York is a global hub of Broadway shows, soaring skyscrapers, iconic neighborhoods, and bustling energy.

overview.tips: Swipe with OMNY at subway turnstiles. Stand on the right side of escalators. Book Broadway show tickets at the TKTS booth for discounts.

hotels.name: The Freehand New York
hotels.highlight: Artistic vibe, gorgeous rooftop bar (Broken Shaker), centrally located.

hotels.name: Pod 39 Hotel
hotels.highlight: Tiny but high-tech budget rooms, rooftop brick courtyard views.

hotels.name: The Plaza Hotel
hotels.highlight: Historic five-star luxury hotel, located next to Central Park.

spots.name: Times Square
spots.highlight: The crossroads of the world. Neon billboard lights that never turn off.

spots.name: Central Park
spots.highlight: 843 acres of green lawns, lakes, pathways, and the Bethesda Fountain.

spots.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
spots.highlight: Historic symbol of freedom. Book crown tickets months in advance.

spots.name: Empire State Building
spots.highlight: Art Deco skyscraper offering high views of Manhattan's skyline.

spots.name: The High Line & Chelsea Market
spots.highlight: Elevated public park built on a historic freight rail line.

schedule.activity: Take the ferry from Battery Park to Liberty Island to see Lady Liberty close up, then visit Ellis Island immigration museum.
Walk through Wall Street, see the Charging Bull, and pay respect at the Twin Reflection Pools of the 9/11 Memorial.
Go up the Empire State Building for sunset, then walk into the neon chaos of Times Square for dinner and a Broadway show.
Rent a bike to tour the park. Check out Bow Bridge, Bethesda Fountain, and pay respects at Strawberry Fields (John Lennon memorial).
Explore 6 floors of legendary modern art, including Van Gogh's Starry Night and Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans.
Stroll down the elevated park, end up at Chelsea Market for tacos or lobster rolls, and enjoy drinks in the Meatpacking District.
Walk across the wooden planks of Brooklyn Bridge from Manhattan side. Capture spectacular photos of the suspension cables.
Get the famous Washington Street photo spot (Bridge framed by buildings), grab pizza at Grimaldi's, and walk along Brooklyn Heights Promenade.
Experience NYC's newest immersive deck: mirror rooms, balloon exhibits, and glass ledges hanging over Grand Central Station.

rome.description: The Eternal City boasts nearly 3,000 years of globally influential art, architecture, and ruins, layered under a lively modern European capital.

overview.tips: Wear shoes fit for cobblestones. Bring a reusable bottle to fill at public fountains (Nasoni). Do not order Cappuccino after 11 AM.

hotels.name: Singer Palace Hotel
hotels.highlight: Boutique art-deco hotel, rooftop terrace looking out at the historic domes.

hotels.name: Hotel Santa Maria
hotels.highlight: Charming former convent centered around an orange garden, cozy neighborhood.

hotels.name: The Beehive
hotels.highlight: Organic cafe, friendly garden hostel near Termini Train Station.

spots.name: Colosseum & Roman Forum
spots.highlight: The world's largest ancient amphitheater where gladiators fought.

spots.name: Treví Fountain
spots.highlight: Baroque masterpiece. Toss a coin in to guarantee your return to Rome.

spots.name: Pantheon
spots.highlight: 2,000-year-old temple featuring the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.

spots.name: Vatican Museums & St. Peter's Basilica
spots.highlight: Home of Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel and the heart of Catholic Rome.

spots.name: Trastevere
spots.highlight: Bohemian neighborhood filled with ivy-draped trattorias and busy bars.

schedule.activity: Enter the arena floor of the Colosseum and walk the ancient stones of the Roman Forum where emperors ruled.
Grab pizza by the slice (Pizza al Taglio) in the trendy Monti neighborhood. Explore craft shops and vintage stores.
Walk to the Trevi Fountain, toss your coin, then head to the Spanish Steps to sit and enjoy Italian gelato.
Arrive early to tour the maps gallery, tapestries, and stand in awe of Michelangelo's ceiling fresco in the Sistine Chapel.
Enter the massive basilica, see the Pieta statue, and climb the dome for incredible views of Rome's key layout.
Walk along the Sant'Angelo bridge lined with Bernini angels, watch the sunset over the Tiber, and grab dinner nearby.
Gaze up at the oculus of the Pantheon. Afterward, stroll around the fountains of Piazza Navona and enjoy a morning espresso.
Browse the open-air market stalls selling fruits, spices, and olive oil. Stop at Forno Campo de' Fiori for freshly baked white pizza with mortadella.
Cross the river into Trastevere. Spend the evening wandering cobblestone lanes and sampling carbonara, suppli, and local wines.

udaipur.description: The City of Lakes and the Venice of the East, Udaipur is a romantic destination adorned with palaces, tranquil lakes, and rolling hills.

overview.tips: Take a sunset boat cruise on Lake Pichola. Visit the crystal gallery inside City Palace.

hotels.name: Lake Pichola Hotel
hotels.highlight: Stunning views of the Lake Palace and City Palace, rooftop dining.

hotels.name: Mewar Castle Hostel
hotels.highlight: Budget-friendly rooftop terrace, close to major landmarks.

hotels.name: The Taj Lake Palace
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury palace in the middle of Lake Pichola, reached by private boat.

spots.name: City Palace Udaipur
spots.highlight: Largest palace complex in Rajasthan, blending Rajasthani and Mughal architecture.

spots.name: Lake Pichola
spots.highlight: Beautiful artificial fresh water lake, featuring the iconic Lake Palace.

spots.name: Jagdish Temple
spots.highlight: Large Hindu temple in the middle of the city with beautiful carvings.

schedule.activity: Explore the museums, courtyards, and balconies offering panoramic lake views.
Visit the 17th-century temple and explore the surrounding narrow market streets.
Take a relaxing boat ride during sunset, passing Jag Mandir island.
Walk through the royal courtyard with fountains, lotus pools, and marble pavilions.
Drive up the hill to get a panoramic view of the lakes and the city.
Watch traditional Rajasthani puppet and folk dance show at the lakefront haveli.
Take a short excursion to the complex of 108 temples dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Visit the rural arts and crafts complex depicting lifestyle of local tribes.
Sit on the ghat steps to see City Palace light up over the water, followed by lakeview dinner.

varanasi.description: Varanasi is one of the world's oldest continually inhabited cities and the spiritual capital of India, famous for its sacred ghats along the River Ganges.

overview.tips: Attend the evening Ganga Aarti. Drink water only from sealed bottles. Watch out for boat ride price variations.

hotels.name: Alka Hotel
hotels.highlight: Superb location directly on the main ghat with views of the Ganges.

hotels.name: Bunkedup Hostel
hotels.highlight: Charming heritage building, popular rooftop community space.

hotels.name: BrijRama Palace Heritage Hotel
hotels.highlight: Opulent 18th-century palace on the ghat, classical live music, luxury boat transfers.

spots.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
spots.highlight: The main and most spectacular ghat, where the famous Ganga Aarti takes place.

spots.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
spots.highlight: Famous golden-spire Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.

spots.name: Sarnath
spots.highlight: Peaceful Buddhist site where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma.

schedule.activity: Witness the morning rituals, bathing, and prayers on the riverbanks as the sun rises.
Visit the golden temple and walk through the historic narrow gullies (alleyways).
Watch the spectacular synchronized oil-lamp prayer ritual at Dashashwamedh Ghat.
Visit the Dhamekh Stupa, Sarnath Museum, and the peaceful Japanese & Tibetan temples.
Explore the green university campus and visit the majestic New Vishwanath Temple (Birla Temple).
Walk along the ghats from Assi Ghat to Harishchandra Ghat. Try local Rabri and Lassi.
Cross the river to see the 18th-century sandstone fort and its quirky vintage car museum.
Visit traditional silk weavers and watch how the world-famous Banarasi silk sarees are made.
Enjoy evening music performances on the Assi Ghat platform and grab local street food like Tamatar Chaat.

kochi.description: Kochi (Cochin) is a historical spice port city where Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch, and British influences merge along the Arabian Sea coast.

overview.tips: Take the local government passenger ferry to Fort Kochi; it is extremely cheap and scenic. Buy fresh fish and have it cooked nearby.

hotels.name: Eighth Bastion Boutique Hotel
hotels.highlight: Chic design hotel with Dutch-colonial decor and organic food.

hotels.name: Zostel Fort Kochi
hotels.highlight: Vibrant backpacker social hostel with a cafe, steps from the beach.

hotels.name: Brunton Boatyard
hotels.highlight: 5-star luxury resort set in a historic shipyard, harbour views, sunset cruise.

spots.name: Chinese Fishing Nets
spots.highlight: Iconic land-cantilevered fishing nets operated since the 14th century.

spots.name: Mattancherry Palace
spots.highlight: Also called the Dutch Palace, featuring vibrant murals depicting Hindu epics.

spots.name: Jew Town & Synagogue
spots.highlight: Atmospheric streets selling spices, antiques, and the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth.

schedule.activity: Stroll along Fort Kochi beach, admire the colonial bungalows, and watch fishermen operate the giant Chinese nets.
Visit the oldest European church in India (where Vasco da Gama was buried) and the gothic Santa Cruz Basilica.
Take a boat cruise around the harbour to see dolphins, passing container terminals and colonial islands.
View the royal portraits, palanquins, and stunning traditional Kerala murals.
Explore antique shops and spice warehouses, then see the hand-painted Chinese tiles in the Jewish Synagogue.
Watch the elaborate makeup process followed by traditional Kathakali classical dance at Kerala Kathakali Centre.
Take an excursion south to ride a traditional houseboat (Kettuvallam) through the scenic backwater canals.
Watch the sunset from Marine Drive walkway in modern Ernakulam, and try local Kerala parotta and beef/veg curry.

agra.description: Agra is home to the world's most famous monument of love, the Taj Mahal, and represents the peak of Mughal architectural excellence.

overview.tips: Visit the Taj Mahal at sunrise for the best views and smaller crowds. Taj is closed on Fridays. Beware of aggressive vendors.

hotels.name: Howard Plaza The Fern
hotels.highlight: Eco-friendly boutique hotel, walking distance from the Taj Mahal gate.

hotels.name: Zostel Agra
hotels.highlight: Rooftop terrace overlooking the Taj Mahal outline, social games room.

hotels.name: The Oberoi Amarvilas
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury hotel where every single room offers an uninterrupted view of the Taj Mahal.

spots.name: Taj Mahal
spots.highlight: Stunning white-marble monument built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

spots.name: Agra Fort
spots.highlight: Massive red sandstone walled city that was the main residence of Mughal emperors.

spots.name: Fatehpur Sikri
spots.highlight: Ghost city of red sandstone, built by Emperor Akbar as his capital.

schedule.activity: Enter as gates open. Watch the marble change colors from soft pink to bright white under the morning sun.
Explore the grand palaces, courtyards, and see the octagonal tower where Shah Jahan was imprisoned.
Walk through the gardens across the river to view the sunset behind the Taj Mahal.
Explore the Buland Darwaza gate, Jama Masjid, and the delicate marble tomb of Salim Chishti.
Visit the red sandstone and white marble mausoleum of the greatest Mughal Emperor Akbar.
Walk the bustling streets and try local street food, especially the famous Agra Petha (pumpkin sweet).
Explore the highly detailed tomb, often described as a draft of the Taj Mahal, featuring beautiful stone inlay.
Watch direct descendants of Taj builders practice Pietra Dura marble inlay work.
Stroll down quiet forest trails 500m from the Taj East Gate, offering peaceful views of the domes.

kyoto.description: Kyoto is the cultural heart of Japan, famous for its thousands of classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, Shinto shrines, and traditional wooden houses.

overview.tips: Purchase a Kyoto Bus/Subway Day Pass. Respect local rules in Gion (do not touch Geishas). Rent a kimono for photographs.

hotels.name: Kyoto Granbell Hotel
hotels.highlight: Boutique hotel blending modern design with traditional Japanese elements, steps from tea houses.

hotels.name: Piece Hostel Sanjo
hotels.highlight: Award-winning design hostel with comfortable custom bunk beds, cozy lounge.

hotels.name: Sowaka Ryokan
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury traditional Japanese inn with private zen gardens and Michelin-star dining.

spots.name: Fushimi Inari-taisha
spots.highlight: Famous shrine with path of 10,000 vibrant orange Torii gates climbing the mountain.

spots.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
spots.highlight: Zen temple covered in gold leaf reflecting beautifully on a surrounding pond.

spots.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
spots.highlight: Scenic forest pathway with towering bamboo stalks rustling in the wind.

schedule.activity: Hike through the endless tunnels of vermilion torii gates to avoid the daytime crowds.
Visit the wooden temple stage offering sweeping views of Kyoto. Walk the historic Ninenzaka streets.
Stroll down Shirakawa canal and Hanami-koji street, hope to spot a real Maiko/Geisha.
Witness the gold-clad pavilion gleaming in the morning light next to its mirror pond.
Contemplate the famous dry landscape zen garden containing 15 mysterious stones.
Walk through 'Kyoto's Kitchen' alleyway. Try octopus skewers, soy-milk donuts, and matcha ice cream.
Walk under the soaring green bamboo, and visit the Tenryu-ji Temple zen landscape gardens.
Climb up the trail to see wild Japanese macaques and enjoy views of the river valley.
Enjoy dinner along the narrow riverfront alleyway lined with traditional wooden restaurants.

florence.description: Florence, capital of Italy's Tuscany region, is home to masterpieces of Renaissance art and architecture, including the iconic Duomo dome.

overview.tips: Book Uffizi Gallery tickets in advance. Tap water is safe. Try local Schiacciata sandwich at All'Antico Vinaio.

hotels.name: Hotel FH55 Grand Hotel Mediterraneo
hotels.highlight: Modern rooms along the Arno river, excellent breakfast buffet.

hotels.name: Ostello Bello Firenze
hotels.highlight: Vibrant design hostel, free welcome drink, guest kitchen, close to train station.

hotels.name: Villa Cora
hotels.highlight: Aristocratic 19th-century villa with heated pool and ornate Italian gardens.

spots.name: Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore (Duomo)
spots.highlight: Breathtaking cathedral with Brunelleschi's famous red-tiled dome.

spots.name: Uffizi Gallery
spots.highlight: One of the most famous art museums, holding works of Botticelli, Da Vinci, and Michelangelo.

spots.name: Ponte Vecchio
spots.highlight: Medieval stone closed-spandrel arch bridge lined with jewelry shops.

schedule.activity: Admire the marble facade, step inside the cathedral, and climb Giotto's Bell Tower.
See the outdoor statues and Palazzo Vecchio. Grab a famous Schiacciata sandwich nearby.
Walk across the historic bridge, check out the shop displays, and explore the Oltrarno artisan district.
See Botticelli's 'The Birth of Venus' and Da Vinci's 'Annunciation' inside the former magistrate palace.
Explore the food stalls on the ground floor of the central market, shop for leather goods in San Lorenzo markets.
Climb up the hill to Piazzale Michelangelo to witness the iconic sunset view of the Duomo and Arno river.
See Michelangelo's original masterpiece sculpture 'David' and his unfinished 'Slaves'.
Cross the river to Pitti Palace and explore the vast 16th-century Italian manicured Boboli Gardens.
Savor a traditional Bistecca alla Fiorentina (Tuscan steak) with local Chianti wine at a local trattoria.

manali.description: Manali is a high-altitude Himalayan resort town known as India's adventure capital, offering paragliding, rafting, and stunning mountain treks.

overview.tips: Rent trekking gear from local shops in Vashisht. Hire certified guides for high-altitude passes. Keep rain gear handy.

hotels.name: Solang Valley Resort
hotels.highlight: Surrounded by snow-capped peaks, offering direct access to adventure sports.

hotels.name: Zostel Manali
hotels.highlight: Vibrant backpacker hub located next to apple orchards and starting trails.

hotels.name: Span Resort & Spa
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury riverside resort with private lawns and views of the Beas River.

spots.name: Jogini Waterfalls Trek
spots.highlight: A scenic trek starting from Vashisht base village to a multi-tiered gushing waterfall.

spots.name: Hampta Pass Day Hike
spots.highlight: High-altitude pine valley trek starting from Sethan base village.

spots.name: Solang Valley Adventure Hub
spots.highlight: Base village for paragliding, zorbing, and quad-biking.

schedule.activity: Start the trek from Vashisht temple base village. Climb through pine forests and apple orchards to reach the Jogini Waterfalls.
Relax by the river and enjoy wood-fired pizza at Cafe 1947.
Head to Solang Valley base village to enjoy paragliding, zip-lining, and scenic views of glaciers.
Drive to Sethan base village. Start a guided day hike climbing towards the snowline of Hampta Pass.
Have a packed lunch on the ridge overlooking the snow peaks of the Pir Panjal range.
Wander Old Manali's rustic village lanes, shop for hand-woven shawls, and relax with live music.
Drive to Gulaba base village and trek through high alpine meadows with panoramic mountain vistas.
Visit the roaring Rahala Waterfalls, formed by melting glaciers amidst dense silver birch woods.
Join white water rafting starting from Pirdi base village down the Beas river rapids.

mumbai.description: The City of Dreams — India's financial capital and Bollywood heartland, where colonial architecture meets buzzing beaches, street food, and relentless energy.

overview.tips: Use local trains for fast travel. Visit Gateway of India at dawn. Try Vada Pav from street stalls. Elephanta Caves ferries leave from Apollo Bunder.

hotels.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
hotels.highlight: Iconic luxury facing the Gateway of India with heritage suites, pool, and legendary service.

hotels.name: Abode Bombay Boutique Hotel
hotels.highlight: Stylish boutique hotel with vintage Bombay-era decor and rooftop lounge.

hotels.name: Zostel Mumbai
hotels.highlight: Budget hostel steps from the Gateway with a vibrant social space.

spots.name: Gateway of India
spots.highlight: The grand basalt arch built to commemorate King George V's visit, overlooking the Arabian Sea.

spots.name: Marine Drive (Queen's Necklace)
spots.highlight: 3km curved boulevard along the sea, stunning at dusk when the streetlights create a necklace of light.

spots.name: Elephanta Caves
spots.highlight: UNESCO rock-cut caves on an island, featuring massive Shiva sculptures from the 5th–8th century.

spots.name: Dharavi Slum & Pottery Town
spots.highlight: Asia's largest informal economy — vibrant pottery, leather, and recycling industries in narrow lanes.

spots.name: Colaba Causeway Market
spots.highlight: Street market with antiques, clothes, handicrafts, and the famous Leopold Cafe nearby.

schedule.spot: Gateway of India & Taj Mahal Palace
schedule.activity: Start at dawn at the Gateway of India. Photograph the Taj Mahal Palace hotel facade across the road.
Take the ferry from Apollo Bunder to Elephanta Island. Explore the rock-cut Shiva caves and UNESCO heritage sculptures.
Walk the Queen's Necklace at sunset and dusk. Watch the sea from the promenade with chaat snacks.
Take a guided walk through Dharavi's thriving kumbharwada pottery colony and leather workshops.
Marvel at the UNESCO Victorian Gothic railway station — one of the world's busiest and most ornate train stations.
Bargain for vintage items, jewellery and handicrafts at the famous street market, end at Leopold Cafe.
Drive across the iconic cable-stayed Sea Link. Explore Bandra's hip cafes, street art, and Bandstand promenade.
Visit one of the most visited temples in India, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, always buzzing with devotees.
Walk Juhu beach at sunset. Try the famous bhel puri, pav bhaji and sugarcane juice from the stalls.

delhi.description: India's capital city — a living museum of empires, where Mughal tombs, British boulevards, and chaotic bazaars coexist with modern diplomatic grandeur.

overview.tips: Use the Delhi Metro to avoid traffic. Old Delhi is best explored on foot or cycle-rickshaw. Book Jama Masjid non-Friday visits.

hotels.name: The Imperial New Delhi
hotels.highlight: 1930s colonial luxury hotel on Janpath with art galleries, multiple restaurants, and a legendary spa.

hotels.name: Haveli Dharampura
hotels.highlight: Restored 200-year-old haveli in Old Delhi with Mughal-era architecture and rooftop dining.

hotels.name: Moustache Delhi Hostel
hotels.highlight: Award-winning hostel with clean dorms, rooftop café, and free walking tour pick-up.

spots.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
spots.highlight: Massive red sandstone Mughal fort where the Independence flag is hoisted every August 15.

spots.name: India Gate
spots.highlight: War memorial arch on Rajpath, surrounded by lawns where families picnic in the evenings.

spots.name: Humayun's Tomb
spots.highlight: UNESCO Mughal garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal — serene, symmetrical, and far less crowded.

spots.name: Qutub Minar
spots.highlight: World's tallest brick minaret (73m), surrounded by the atmospheric ruins of Delhi's oldest mosque.

spots.name: Chandni Chowk
spots.highlight: 17th-century Mughal market street — the best place for paranthe, spices, wedding fabric, and street chaos.

schedule.activity: Start at UNESCO-listed Humayun's Tomb, then walk through the lush Lodhi Garden with ancient monuments.
Walk the grand boulevard. Visit the Eternal Flame and see Parliament House from Rajpath.
Explore India's most famous circular market, have dinner at a heritage restaurant like Kwality or Wenger's.
Take a cycle-rickshaw through Old Delhi's spice lanes. Climb the minarets of Jama Masjid for a panorama.
Explore the massive Mughal fort with the Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, and Mumtaz Mahal museum.
Browse the eclectic art galleries, cafes, and boutiques set around a 14th-century reservoir and deer park.
Explore the minaret, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, and the mysterious Iron Pillar that has not rusted in 1,600 years.
Visit the stunning contemporary Hindu temple complex with boat ride exhibitions and fountains.
Browse artisan stalls from every Indian state. Try regional food from Rajasthan, Bengal, and the Northeast.

goa.description: India's beach party capital — where Portuguese colonial churches, sun-bleached sands, cashew feni, and sunset boat parties meet tropical rainforests and spice plantations.

overview.tips: Rent a scooter — it's the best way to get around. North Goa is for parties, South Goa for peace. Avoid peak Christmas-New Year unless booked months ahead.

hotels.name: Taj Exotica Goa
hotels.highlight: Portuguese-estate luxury resort on a secluded beach with private pools, butler service, and sea views.

hotels.name: Pousada by the Beach
hotels.highlight: Boutique beachside hotel with a tropical garden pool and authentic Goan cuisine.

hotels.name: Jungle By The Creek Hostel
hotels.highlight: Treehouse-style eco-hostel in the jungle, 10 minutes from Anjuna beach with hammocks and bonfires.

spots.name: Baga Beach
spots.highlight: North Goa's most iconic beach strip with shacks, watersports, and legendary nightlife.

spots.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
spots.highlight: UNESCO Baroque church housing the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, a pilgrimage site since 1605.

spots.name: Dudhsagar Waterfalls
spots.highlight: India's tallest waterfall (310m), a four-tier cascade in the heart of Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary.

spots.name: Anjuna Flea Market
spots.highlight: Famous Wednesday hippie market with boho clothes, vintage goods, silver jewellery, and live music.

spots.name: Palolem Beach
spots.highlight: South Goa's most beautiful crescent beach — calm waters, kayaks, and silent disco parties at night.

schedule.activity: Visit the UNESCO Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral — grand 16th-century Portuguese baroque churches.
Spend the afternoon on Baga Beach. Try parasailing, ride banana boats, or simply relax under a shack umbrella.
Experience Goa's famous nightlife strip — beach shack dinners, live music, and open-air clubs.
Join a full-day jeep safari through the Goan jungle to reach the magnificent Dudhsagar Falls. Swim in the pool.
Visit a spice plantation near Ponda. See vanilla, pepper, nutmeg and cardamom growing wild, and eat a Goan thali.
Browse the famous Wednesday market for boho fashion, silver jewellery, tribal art, and organic products.
Hike up to Chapora Fort (made famous by 'Dil Chahta Hai') for sweeping views over the Vagator beaches.
Drive south to the crescent sands of Palolem. Watch the sunset with a fresh coconut or join a silent disco.

rishikesh.description: The Yoga Capital of the World — a holy Himalayan town on the Ganges where pilgrims, thrill-seekers, and spiritual wanderers share the same riverbank.

overview.tips: Alcohol and meat are banned on the holy riverbanks. Go white-water rafting from Shivpuri. Laxman Jhula is always crowded — visit at 6am for peace.

hotels.name: Aloha on the Ganges
hotels.highlight: Tented luxury resort directly on the Ganges bank with yoga sessions and forest spa.

hotels.name: The Bunk Hostel Rishikesh
hotels.highlight: Social hostel near Laxman Jhula with riverside yoga, café, and trip bookings.

hotels.name: Atali Ganga River Camp
hotels.highlight: Riverside camping resort with bonfire, rafting packages, and starlit Ganges views.

spots.name: Laxman Jhula Suspension Bridge
spots.highlight: The iconic iron suspension bridge over the turquoise Ganges, surrounded by temples and cafes.

spots.name: Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia)
spots.highlight: Abandoned ashram where The Beatles famously meditated in 1968 — covered in stunning mural street art.

spots.name: Triveni Ghat Morning Aarti
spots.highlight: Most sacred ghat in Rishikesh — witness the evening Ganga Aarti fire ceremony at dusk.

spots.name: Shivpuri White Water Rafting
spots.highlight: Grade II-IV rapids on a 16km stretch of the Ganges — the best rafting experience in India.

spots.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
spots.highlight: Ancient hilltop Shiva temple 32km from Rishikesh through dense forest — a pilgrimage through pristine nature.

schedule.activity: Witness the sacred Ganga Aarti ceremony at sunrise. Take a dip or simply sit by the river and meditate.
Cross the hanging bridges, explore the riverside temples, shops, and rooftop cafes with Ganges views.
Explore the abandoned ashram made famous by The Beatles — covered in massive murals and wall art.
Join a guided rafting trip from Shivpuri covering 16km of Grade II-IV rapids on the Ganges.
Attend a 2-hour hatha yoga session at Parmarth Niketan Ashram overlooking the Ganges.
Attend the most spectacular Aarti in Rishikesh — thousands of oil lamps float on the sacred river.
Hire a shared cab or trek through the forest to the ancient hilltop Shiva temple 32km away.
Spot wild elephants, tigers, and leopards on a jeep safari in Rajaji forest — just 20km from Rishikesh.
Camp on the Ganges bank with a bonfire, stargazing, and the sound of the river — the perfect Rishikesh end.

amritsar.description: The holiest city of the Sikhs — home to the transcendent Golden Temple, a moving Wagah Border ceremony, and the most deeply flavourful Punjabi food on earth.

overview.tips: Cover your head and remove shoes at the Golden Temple. The langar (free community meal) serves 100,000 people daily — eat there. Book Wagah Border seats by 5pm.

hotels.name: Taj Swarna Amritsar
hotels.highlight: Luxury hotel a few minutes walk from the Golden Temple with a heritage-inspired spa.

hotels.name: Mrs. Bhandari's Guesthouse
hotels.highlight: Legendary heritage guesthouse famous in backpacker circles — colonial bungalow with garden.

hotels.name: Moustache Hostel Amritsar
hotels.highlight: Clean hostel with bicycle rental, walking tour bookings, and amazing rooftop views of the old city.

spots.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
spots.highlight: The most sacred Sikh shrine — a golden sanctuary floating in a sacred pool, spiritual 24 hours a day.

spots.name: Wagah Border Ceremony
spots.highlight: The electrifying daily lowering of flags at the India-Pakistan border — 20,000 spectators, military pageantry.

spots.name: Jallianwala Bagh
spots.highlight: Memorial garden site of the 1919 British massacre — harrowing bullet marks still visible on the walls.

spots.name: Partition Museum
spots.highlight: The world's first museum dedicated to the 1947 Partition — deeply moving personal testimonies and artefacts.

spots.name: Kesar da Dhaba
spots.highlight: Founded in 1916 — the most famous and authentic Amritsari food stall serving dal makhani and kulcha.

schedule.activity: Experience the breathtaking pre-dawn palki sahib ceremony where the Guru Granth Sahib is ceremonially placed.
Eat a free meal in the world's largest community kitchen alongside pilgrims, volunteers, and travellers.
Pay respects at the massacre site and spend 2 hours in the deeply moving Partition Museum.
Arrive early to get a front-row seat for the iconic India-Pakistan flag-lowering ceremony.
Dine at the 100-year-old dhaba for the most authentic Amritsari dal makhani, paneer bhurji, and kulcha.
Visit the Hindu mirror temple styled like the Golden Temple, then stroll the Maharaja Ranjit Singh museum garden.
Eat your way through Amritsar's famous food street — lassi at Gian da Dhaba, kulchas, and pinni sweets.
Return to the Golden Temple at night when the golden facade reflects in the sacred pool — the most beautiful view.

leh.description: The Land of High Passes — a stark, otherworldly Himalayan desert at 3,500m where turquoise lakes, ancient Buddhist monasteries, and snow-capped peaks create the earth's most dramatic landscape.

overview.tips: Rest for the first 2 days after arriving (acclimatize to altitude). Carry a doctor's prescription for Diamox. Download offline maps — internet is scarce. Permits are needed for Pangong & Nubra.

hotels.name: The Grand Dragon Ladakh
hotels.highlight: Premier Ladakhi hotel with heated rooms, mountain view restaurant, and expedition planning services.

hotels.name: Stok Palace Heritage Hotel
hotels.highlight: Stay in a royal 200-year-old palace of the Namgyal dynasty with panoramic mountain views.

hotels.name: Zostel Leh
hotels.highlight: Budget hostel with Himalayan view rooftop, traveller community, and jeep tour bookings.

spots.name: Pangong Lake
spots.highlight: The stunning 134km-long high-altitude saltwater lake changing from turquoise to blue to sapphire — part in India, part in China.

spots.name: Nubra Valley
spots.highlight: A dramatic valley with Bactrian double-hump camels on sand dunes against Himalayan peaks — surreal and beautiful.

spots.name: Khardung La Pass
spots.highlight: One of the world's highest motorable passes (5,359m) — drive to the rooftop of the world.

spots.name: Thiksey Monastery
spots.highlight: 12-story Tibetan-style monastery with a colossal Maitreya Buddha and panoramic views — resembles Potala Palace in Lhasa.

spots.name: Magnetic Hill
spots.highlight: Optical illusion where vehicles appear to roll uphill — an eerie natural phenomenon on the Leh-Kargil highway.

schedule.activity: Acclimatize slowly. Visit the ruined 17th-century Leh Palace, then hike up to the white Shanti Stupa for a 360° panorama.
Browse the main bazaar for Tibetan jewellery, pashmina, and dried apricots. Then visit Hemis, Ladakh's largest monastery.
Return to the Leh Palace hilltop for the golden sunset over the valley and Stok Kangri glacier.
Drive via Chang La pass to Pangong Lake. Watch the colours change across the lake. Overnight camping or return by evening.
Drive up to Khardung La (5,359m). Photograph the world's highest motorable road sign and see glaciers.

schedule.spot: Nubra Valley Sand Dunes & Camel Safari
schedule.activity: Descend into Nubra Valley to ride Bactrian camels on sand dunes backed by snow mountains.
Visit the 14th-century Diskit Monastery. Witness the evening prayers and see the 32m Maitreya Buddha statue.

jodhpur.description: The Blue City — a walled medieval city painted cobalt blue, dominated by the most imposing fort in Rajputana, and famous for its spicy meat curries and mirror-worked textiles.

overview.tips: Walk the narrow blue lanes of the old city early morning. Visit Mehrangarh from the back entrance for free sunrise views. Try laal maas (red mutton curry) for dinner.

hotels.name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
hotels.highlight: One of the world's largest private homes — a 347-room art deco palace hotel still home to the royal family.

hotels.name: Pal Haveli Heritage Hotel
hotels.highlight: Restored 450-year-old haveli with rooftop restaurant directly facing Mehrangarh Fort — stunning views.

hotels.name: Cosy Guest House Jodhpur
hotels.highlight: Budget guesthouse deep in the blue city with a rooftop terrace overlooking the old city maze.

spots.name: Mehrangarh Fort
spots.highlight: The most majestic fort in Rajasthan — rising 125m over the blue city with immaculate palace interiors and museum.

spots.name: Jaswant Thada Cenotaph
spots.highlight: Delicate white marble memorial to Maharaja Jaswant Singh II — nicknamed the 'Taj Mahal of Marwar'.

spots.name: Clock Tower & Sardar Market
spots.highlight: The old city's beating heart — a vibrant bazaar selling spices, tie-dye fabrics, antiques, and jodhpuri mojaris.

spots.name: Mandore Gardens
spots.highlight: Ancient capital of Marwar, with royal cenotaphs and a museum set in lush gardens — uncrowded and peaceful.

spots.name: Osian Desert Safari
spots.highlight: 65km from Jodhpur — camel safaris and sand dunes at the ruins of ancient Osian Jain and Hindu temples.

schedule.activity: Spend the morning in Mehrangarh — the best fort in India. Explore the Moti Mahal, Phool Mahal, and museum.
schedule.transport: Cab or walk from old city

schedule.activity: Visit the marble cenotaph and the royal museum at Umaid Bhawan Palace — Rolls-Royces, weapons, clocks.
Wander through the narrow indigo-painted lanes of the old city. Shop at Sardar Market and climb the clock tower.
Drive to the desert town of Osian for camel rides, sand dunes, and the 8th-century Osian Sachiya Mata temple complex.
Visit the ancient former capital of Marwar with its royal cenotaphs, Hall of Heroes sculptures, and museum.
Walk around the serene artificial lake from 1159 AD, surrounded by a mango and papaya orchard.
Return to the fort ramparts for sunset — the blue city glows gold and the whole Thar Desert panorama unfolds.

darjeeling.description: The Queen of the Hills — a misty tea-garden hill station on the lower Himalayas where the toy train whistles through clouds, and Kangchenjunga glows pink at dawn.

overview.tips: Book the Tiger Hill jeep by 3:30am for sunrise views. Visit tea gardens in the morning when picking is active. The toy train is a must-ride.

hotels.name: The Elgin Darjeeling
hotels.highlight: 1887 colonial heritage hotel with fireplaces, tea-time rituals, and mountain-view verandas.

hotels.name: Hotel Dekeling
hotels.highlight: Charming Tibetan-style guesthouse with excellent views of Kangchenjunga from the breakfast room.

hotels.name: Zostel Darjeeling
hotels.highlight: Hillside backpacker hostel with a stunning mountain-view deck and community bonfires.

spots.name: Tiger Hill Sunrise
spots.highlight: At dawn, watch Kangchenjunga (world's 3rd highest peak) turn gold-pink and pink-orange — Mt. Everest visible on clear days.

spots.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train)
spots.highlight: UNESCO World Heritage steam toy train — the most scenic short-rail journey in the world through tea gardens and clouds.

spots.name: Batasia Loop
spots.highlight: Famous spiral railway loop where the toy train spirals downhill — beautiful Kangchenjunga backdrop.

spots.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate
spots.highlight: Walk through the oldest Darjeeling tea estate (1854) and watch the plucking, withering and fermenting process.

spots.name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoo
spots.highlight: World-famous zoo specialising in high-altitude animals — snow leopard, Siberian tiger, and red panda.

schedule.activity: Drive up to Tiger Hill viewpoint. Watch Kangchenjunga and Everest glow with the first light of dawn.
Stop at Batasia Loop war memorial, then board the UNESCO toy train for a morning joy ride through the hills.
Walk through the tea gardens in the afternoon picking hour. Buy fresh first-flush Darjeeling tea directly.
Visit the Himalayan Zoo to see snow leopards and red pandas, then the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute museum.
Visit the oldest Buddhist monastery in Darjeeling (1875). See the 4.5m Maitreya Buddha inside.
Walk Darjeeling's famous pedestrian mall. Eat momos and thukpa, watch the clouds roll in below the ridge.
Visit the oldest tea estate in Darjeeling (1859). Walk the biodynamic fields with a guide, then tea-tasting session.
Take the Darjeeling Rangit Valley Ropeway for sweeping views over the Teesta and Rangit rivers.
Browse the hillside bookshop then head to Glenary's Bakery & Restaurant — Darjeeling's most loved café since 1935.

mysuru.description: The City of Palaces — a royal Karnataka city of sandalwood, silk sarees, yoga, and the most opulent maharaja's palace in India, lit by 100,000 bulbs each Sunday.

overview.tips: Visit Mysore Palace on Sunday evenings when 100,000 lights illuminate it. Buy genuine Mysore Silk sarees from the Government Silk Factory. Visit Chamundi Hills at dusk.

hotels.name: Lalitha Mahal Palace Hotel
hotels.highlight: Converted royal banquet palace of the Wodeyar dynasty — ornate domes, billiard rooms, and formal gardens.

hotels.name: Royal Orchid Metropole
hotels.highlight: Heritage 1920s colonial hotel near the palace with garden dining and old-world Mysore atmosphere.

hotels.name: Zostel Mysore
hotels.highlight: Clean budget hostel with bicycle rentals, game room, and guided heritage walks.

spots.name: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
spots.highlight: The most visited monument in India after the Taj Mahal — a 1912 Indo-Saracenic masterpiece of stained glass, gold, and carvings.

spots.name: Chamundi Hills
spots.highlight: Sacred hilltop temple complex with 1,000 steps, Nandi bull, and a panorama of the palace-studded city below.

spots.name: Brindavan Gardens
spots.highlight: One of India's most beautiful terraced gardens with musical fountain shows at night below the KRS dam.

spots.name: Devaraja Market
spots.highlight: A feast for the senses — 150-year-old market with jasmine garlands, sandalwood incense, turmeric, and silk.

spots.name: Srirangapatna Fort Island
spots.highlight: River island fort where Tipu Sultan made his last stand in 1799 — dungeons, mosque, and summer palace intact.

schedule.activity: Arrive at the palace before crowds. Marvel at the Kalyana Mantapa (wedding hall), golden throne, and Dussehra paintings.
Immerse in the 150-year-old bazaar. Buy jasmine strings, rose water, and Mysore agarbatti (incense).
Watch as 100,000 light bulbs turn the palace golden — a mesmerising spectacle visible from kilometres away.
Either climb the 1,000 steps or drive up. Visit the Chamundeshwari Devi temple and see the ancient Nandi bull statue.
Explore Tipu Sultan's island fort, Ranganathaswamy temple, the Gumbaz mausoleum, and the summer palace Daria Daulat.
Drive 20km to KRS dam for the colourful musical fountain show among the terraced Mughal-style gardens.
Visit the Government Silk Factory to see weavers working on giant looms creating iconic Mysore silk sarees.
Walk or cycle around the peaceful lakeside bird sanctuary inside a butterfly park with resident painted storks.
Visit the magnificent neo-Gothic twin-spired church built in 1933, inspired by Cologne Cathedral.

hampi.description: The Ruins of an Empire — a UNESCO World Heritage landscape of extraordinary boulder-strewn plains, where the colossal ruins of the medieval Vijayanagara empire stretch for kilometres.

overview.tips: Rent a bicycle or moped to cover the ruins. Visit Matanga Hill for a sunrise 360° view over the temple tops. Hippie Island (Virupapur Gadde) across the river is the backpacker hangout.

hotels.name: Evolve Back Kamalapura Palace
hotels.highlight: Ultra-luxury heritage resort built to resemble the Lotus Mahal, with a pool and curated ruins tours.

hotels.name: Kishkinda Heritage Resort
hotels.highlight: Eco-resort in the ancient kingdom of Kishkinda across the river — boulders, greenery, and total peace.

hotels.name: Mowgli Guest House
hotels.highlight: Iconic backpacker guesthouse on Hippie Island with hammocks, river view, and nightly bonfires.

spots.name: Virupaksha Temple
spots.highlight: The only temple still in active worship in Hampi — a 7th-century Shiva temple with a 50m tower and resident elephant.

spots.name: Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
spots.highlight: The most magnificent temple complex in Hampi — musical pillars that produce musical notes when tapped, and the iconic stone chariot.

spots.name: Lotus Mahal
spots.highlight: The most elegant building in Hampi — a delicate pavilion of lotus-shaped arches built for the royal zenana.

spots.name: Matanga Hill Sunrise
spots.highlight: A 30-minute boulder-scramble to the top rewards with a 360° panorama over the entire Hampi ruins at sunrise.

spots.name: Tungabhadra River Coracle Ride
spots.highlight: Ride a traditional circular coracle boat across the Tungabhadra River to reach Hippie Island.

schedule.activity: Trek up Matanga Hill (45 mins) to watch the sun rise over the temple towers and boulders — totally worth it.
Get a blessing from Lakshmi the temple elephant. Explore the bazaar street and the sacred tank.
Visit the crown jewel of Hampi — tap the musical pillars and photograph the stone chariot at golden hour.
Explore the Zenana enclosure, Elephant Stables, Lotus Mahal, and the Hazara Rama temple's incredible frieze carvings.
Walk among the cluster of pre-Vijayanagara temples on Hemakuta Hill with city views and few tourists.
Cross to Virupapur Gadde on a coracle. Watch the sunset from the Island Chai Shop — the best view in Hampi.
Cross the river to ancient Kishkinda (Anegundi). Climb Anjaneya Hill (monkey temple) — said to be Hanuman's birthplace.
Walk the ruined medieval bazaar street and descend into the flooded underground Shivalinga temple.
Climb to the top of Virupaksha Tower for the most beautiful view of the sun setting over the ruins.

bali.description: The Island of the Gods — terraced emerald rice fields, a thousand flower-decorated Hindu temples, world-class surf breaks, and the most serene sunrise you will ever witness over a caldera lake.

overview.tips: Rent a scooter in Ubud. Dress modestly at temples (sarongs available at entrance). Book Tegalalang and Uluwatu at early morning or late afternoon for no crowds. Card skimming is common — use cash.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Bali at Sayan
hotels.highlight: Jungle treetop luxury resort suspended over a river gorge — private pool villas and morning mist yoga.

hotels.name: Komaneka at Bisma
hotels.highlight: Boutique cliffside resort over the Wos River valley with rice terrace views and a rooftop infinity pool.

hotels.name: Canggu Backpackers Hostel
hotels.highlight: Social surf hostel in hip Canggu with a pool, weekly events, and steps to the beach.

spots.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
spots.highlight: UNESCO-listed ancient subak irrigation system — layers of vivid emerald rice paddies cascading down a hillside.

spots.name: Tanah Lot Temple
spots.highlight: Ancient sea temple perched on a dramatic coastal rock — most photographed at sunset over the Indian Ocean.

spots.name: Uluwatu Cliff Temple & Kecak Fire Dance
spots.highlight: Hindu temple atop 70m cliffs — the sunset Kecak fire dance performance here is an unmissable spectacle.

spots.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
spots.highlight: Night hike up an active volcano to watch sunrise over the caldera lake and mountains — an extraordinary experience.

spots.name: Tirta Gangga Water Palace
spots.highlight: Royal water palace of the Karangasem kings with elaborate fountains, stepping stones, and tiered pools.

schedule.activity: Guided night hike up Mount Batur active volcano (1,717m). Cook eggs in volcanic steam at the summit. Sunrise is incredible.
Walk the iconic rice terrace paths in the afternoon light. Swing on the jungle swing for a photo.
Walk through the ancient forest with 700+ macaque monkeys, three 14th-century temples, and old-growth trees.
Visit the Puri Saren royal palace courtyard, then browse Ubud Art Market for silver, batik, and woodcarvings.
Drive east to the Water Palace. Walk among the stepping stones, ornamental carp ponds, and tiered fountains.
Watch the Kecak fire dance at sunset on the Uluwatu cliff — one of the most dramatic performances in Asia.
Visit the sea temple on a coastal rock at high morning tide when it's completely surrounded by ocean.
Spend the afternoon on Seminyak's fashionable beach strip with beach clubs, surf, and boutique shopping.
Watch the Balinese sunset from Ku De Ta or Potato Head beach club with cocktails.

bangkok.description: The City of Angels — a frenetic, sensory-overloading Asian mega-city where golden temples and royal palaces share blocks with night markets, rooftop bars, and the world's greatest street food.

overview.tips: Use the BTS Skytrain and MRT to avoid traffic. Dress modestly at temples (no shorts). Try pad thai and mango sticky rice from street stalls. Visit temples early morning before the heat.

hotels.name: Mandarin Oriental Bangkok
hotels.highlight: A legendary 1876 riverside hotel — the most storied address in Asia, with bespoke butler service.

hotels.name: Ariyasom Villa
hotels.highlight: Serene Art Deco villa retreat with a lotus pond and organic vegan Thai restaurant — an urban sanctuary.

hotels.name: NapPark Hostel Khao San
hotels.highlight: Capsule-pod hostel with AC and lockers on the legendary Khao San backpacker strip.

spots.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
spots.highlight: The most sacred site in Thailand — a golden compound of spires, Buddha sculptures, and gleaming mosaic demons.

spots.name: Wat Pho (Reclining Buddha)
spots.highlight: The 46m gold-plated Reclining Buddha and Thailand's oldest temple — also the birthplace of traditional Thai massage.

spots.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
spots.highlight: The iconic porcelain-inlaid spire temple on the west bank of the Chao Phraya — most beautiful at sunset across the river.

spots.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
spots.highlight: The original floating market — vendors in wooden boats selling tropical fruits, pad thai, and papaya salad on canals.

spots.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
spots.highlight: One of the world's largest weekend markets — 15,000 stalls selling clothes, antiques, plants, street food, and art.

schedule.activity: Arrive early for the Grand Palace compound. Marvel at the golden Temple of the Emerald Buddha.
See the enormous gold Reclining Buddha, then book a 1-hour traditional massage at the temple's massage school.
Cross the river by ferry to watch the sun set behind the towering Temple of Dawn — the perfect Bangkok shot.
Go early before tour buses arrive. Hire a long-tail boat to explore the canals and buy fresh fruit from boat vendors.
Spend the afternoon in the massive weekend market — best for vintage fashion, art prints, local ceramics, and Thai snacks.
Experience the legendary backpacker street — street food, fire shows, live music, and mango smoothies.
Walk or jog through Bangkok's green lung — watch Thais doing Tai Chi, see giant monitor lizards in the lake.
Tour the extraordinary Asian art collection of American silk entrepreneur Jim Thompson in his 6-house Thai mansion.
Have a drink on the 63rd floor Sirocco Sky Bar — Bangkok's most famous rooftop open-air bar with a 360° city panorama.

singapore.description: The Lion City — a spotlessly clean, staggeringly efficient city-state where futuristic Supertrees tower over ancient Peranakan shophouses, and a world-class hawker stall can earn a Michelin star.

overview.tips: Use the EZ-Link card on the MRT — it's clean, fast, and cheap. Eat at hawker centres for 1-Michelin-star quality at $3-5 per plate. Jay Chou's birthplace district Chinatown is unmissable.

hotels.name: Marina Bay Sands
hotels.highlight: The world's most iconic hotel — infinity pool on a sky park spanning three towers, 57 floors up.

hotels.name: Capella Singapore
hotels.highlight: The most glamorous resort in Singapore — colonial estate on a private Sentosa bay with butler service.

hotels.name: The Pod @ Beach Road
hotels.highlight: Smart capsule hostel with individual pods, AC, privacy screens, and a rooftop terrace.

spots.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
spots.highlight: The infinity pool and observation deck on top of three 55-storey towers — the most recognisable skyline in Asia.

spots.name: Gardens by the Bay
spots.highlight: 18 Supertrees and two giant conservatories (Flower Dome and Cloud Forest) — a breathtaking urban garden spectacle.

spots.name: Sentosa Island Beaches
spots.highlight: Singapore's tropical resort island — beaches, Universal Studios, S.E.A. Aquarium, and the Wings of Time show.

spots.name: Chinatown & Maxwell Food Centre
spots.highlight: Award-winning hawker centre housing the Michelin-starred Tian Tian chicken rice stall — Singapore food culture in a bowl.

spots.name: Little India & Tekka Market
spots.highlight: The most colourful district in Singapore — golden temples, jasmine garlands, sari shops, and Indian street food.

schedule.activity: Visit the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest, then walk among the 25m-tall Supertrees. Incredible at any hour.
Walk the waterfront promenade past the Helix Bridge, the Esplanade, and Merlion Park for the iconic skyline shot.
Watch the nightly Garden Rhapsody light and music show under the glowing Supertrees — completely free.
Explore the Chinatown Heritage Centre, then eat the Michelin-starred chicken rice at Tian Tian.
Immerse in the most sensory district — jasmine, spice, and sari shops. Visit the vibrant Hindu temple.
Dine or drink along the neon-lit Clarke Quay waterfront — Singapore's most vibrant nightlife area.
Take the cable car to Sentosa Island. Visit Universal Studios, or simply relax at Palawan Beach.
Walk Singapore's famous luxury shopping boulevard, then ascend the ION Orchard Observation Deck for city views.

seoul.description: K-Culture Capital — a dynamic mega-city where ancient five-century-old palaces and Buddhist temples coexist with K-pop neon arcades, beauty boutiques, and the world's fastest internet.

overview.tips: Get a T-money card for the metro. Try Gwangjang Market for live sannakji (octopus) and bindaetteok. Visit Bukchon on weekdays to avoid crowds. Korean BBQ always with soju.

hotels.name: The Shilla Seoul
hotels.highlight: Seoul's most legendary luxury hotel — palatial rooms, a designer spa, and views over Namsan Mountain.

hotels.name: Ryse Hotel Autograph
hotels.highlight: Art-forward designer hotel in the hipster Hongdae district with a rooftop pool and gallery spaces.

hotels.name: Zaza Backpackers Hostel Hongdae
hotels.highlight: Vibrant budget hostel in the university nightlife district steps from live music clubs and street art.

spots.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
spots.highlight: The great Northern Palace of the Joseon dynasty — guard-changing ceremony, hanbok rentals, and a stunning mountain backdrop.

spots.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
spots.highlight: 600-year-old urban village of traditional Korean hanok houses on narrow lanes overlooking the modern city.

spots.name: Namsan Tower (N Seoul Tower)
spots.highlight: The romantic cable-car-accessed communication tower on Namsan Mountain — city lights panorama and love-lock wall.

spots.name: Myeongdong Shopping District
spots.highlight: The K-beauty capital — thousands of skincare shops, fashion brands, and the most vibrant street food in Seoul.

spots.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
spots.highlight: Zaha Hadid's futuristic curved silver oval — the world's largest seamless structure, hosting design and fashion exhibitions.

schedule.activity: Rent a hanbok for free entry and stunning photographs. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10am and 2pm.
Walk the steep lanes of Bukchon to find the perfect Instagram vista point at Bukchon-ro 11-gil.
Browse the art galleries, tea houses, and craft shops of Insadong. Try traditional hotteok (syrup pancakes).
Take the cable car up Namsan. Walk the summit paths through pine forest with the whole Seoul skyline visible.
Spend the afternoon browsing Korea's biggest beauty and fashion district. Eat tteokbokki from street carts.
Grill samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi at a local restaurant with banchan sides — the quintessential Seoul experience.
Eat bindaetteok pancakes, mayak gimbap (drug rolls), and raw octopus sannakji in Korea's oldest covered market.
Explore Zaha Hadid's silver futuristic building. Browse the design market inside — perfect for souvenir shopping.
Experience the Hongdae university district — street performances, digital art cafes, and the weekly night flea market.

dubai.description: The City of Superlatives — the world's tallest building, largest mall, longest outdoor gold market, and most dramatic desert dunes, all in a single coastal desert emirate.

overview.tips: Dress modestly in malls and public areas. Avoid public affection. Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah are best at night. Friday is the day off — most malls close until noon. Haggle at the Gold Souk.

hotels.name: Burj Al Arab Jumeirah
hotels.highlight: The world's only 7-star hotel on a private artificial island — helipad, underwater restaurant, and a butler per room.

hotels.name: Address Downtown Dubai
hotels.highlight: Luxury tower hotel steps from the Dubai Fountain with Burj Khalifa views from every room.

hotels.name: Rove Downtown Hostel-Hotel
hotels.highlight: Modern mid-range hotel with pool, café, and Dubai Mall access — the best value in Dubai's most central area.

spots.name: Burj Khalifa At the Top
spots.highlight: The world's tallest building (828m) — the observation deck on floors 124 and 148 is the highest public viewing platform on earth.

spots.name: Dubai Mall & Dubai Fountain
spots.highlight: The world's largest mall with an indoor ice rink, aquarium, and the world's tallest choreographed fountain show nightly.

spots.name: Dubai Creek & Gold Souk
spots.highlight: The historic old city of Dubai — ride an abra dhow across the Creek, haggle for gold, and inhale the spice souk.

spots.name: Palm Jumeirah & Atlantis
spots.highlight: The palm-shaped artificial island with its iconic Atlantis resort, private beach, and best sea views of the Dubai skyline.

spots.name: Desert Safari & Bedouin Camp
spots.highlight: Dune-bashing in 4x4s, sandboarding, camel rides, and a Bedouin camp dinner with belly dancing under the stars.

schedule.activity: Cross the Creek on a traditional abra. Explore the Gold Souk (200+ shops), Spice Souk, and Al Fahidi historic district.
Ascend to the 124th floor observation deck. Incredible 360° views over the city, desert, and Gulf.
schedule.transport: Metro Red Line to Burj Khalifa

schedule.activity: Watch the world's largest fountain show from the boardwalk every 30 mins after sunset. Dine in Dubai Mall.
Afternoon 4x4 dune-bashing, sandboarding, camel ride, henna tattooing, and a lavish camp dinner with shows.
Return to stroll the glittering Marina promenade at night — yacht-lined waters and waterfront restaurants.
Take the Palm Monorail to the tip of the Palm. Visit the Atlantis Aquaventure Waterpark or the private beach.
Book the Burj Al Arab's signature afternoon tea in the Sky View Bar — the only way to get inside without a room.

barcelona.description: Gaudí's City — a Mediterranean masterpiece where organic Art Nouveau architecture, white-sand city beaches, Picasso's legacy, and the world's best tapas all meet on the Catalan coast.

overview.tips: Book Sagrada Familia tickets weeks in advance. La Boqueria gets overwhelmingly crowded — go before 10am. Avoid pickpockets on La Rambla. Barcelona Card gives unlimited metro travel.

hotels.name: Hotel Arts Barcelona
hotels.highlight: Luxury Frank Gehry-designed tower on Barceloneta beach with a Michelin-starred restaurant and spectacular sea views.

hotels.name: Casa Camper Barcelona
hotels.highlight: Design boutique hotel with free 24-hour snacks, hammocks in the communal area, and art-district location.

hotels.name: TOC Hostel Barcelona
hotels.highlight: Barcelona's most social hostel with a rooftop pool, bar, and daily events — excellent central location.

spots.name: Sagrada Família
spots.highlight: Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece — the world's most visited construction site, with towers of organic stone still rising since 1882.

spots.name: Park Güell
spots.highlight: Gaudí's mosaic-tiled terraced park with a dragon staircase and the most photographed bench in Barcelona.

spots.name: La Rambla & La Boqueria Market
spots.highlight: Barcelona's famous pedestrian boulevard leading to the world's most colourful covered food market.

spots.name: Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)
spots.highlight: 2,000-year-old Roman-medieval labyrinth — narrow streets of Roman columns, a 14th-century cathedral, and hidden plazas.

spots.name: Barceloneta Beach
spots.highlight: The urban beach just 20 minutes walk from the Gothic Quarter — paella, cava, and Mediterranean sunshine.

schedule.activity: Pre-book tower access to climb the Nativity and Passion facades. The interior stained glass at noon is the most beautiful light show in architecture.
Walk the grid district to see Gaudí's Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Domènech i Montaner's buildings.
Bar-hop the Eixample tapas bars — try patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, pan con tomate, and Catalan cava.
Book the monumental zone ticket in advance. Walk the mosaic dragon staircase and terrace with city views.
Get lost in the ancient Roman-era quarter. Find the Roman temple of Augustus and the Gothic cathedral's rooftop.
Visit Picasso Museum (early evening extended hours), then tapas in the El Born neighbourhood's lantern-lit streets.
Go early before the tourist rush. Eat fresh fruit, jamón, and seafood tapas with locals at the market counter.
Walk from La Barceloneta's fishing quarter to the beach. Have a seafood paella with a sea view.
Tour the home of FC Barcelona — one of the world's most famous stadiums, the museum holds the Ballon d'Or trophies.

london.description: The World's City — where Roman walls, Tudor palaces, Victorian museums, and a world-beating arts and food scene coexist in a grey-skied, red-bussed, relentlessly creative global capital.

overview.tips: Get an Oyster card for the Tube. Most major museums are free. Book popular restaurants weeks ahead. Use Santander Cycles (Boris Bikes). Borough Market is best on Thursday-Saturday.

hotels.name: The Savoy Hotel
hotels.highlight: The legendary 1889 Thames-side hotel — Art Deco grandeur, the American Bar, and impeccable white-glove service.

hotels.name: CitizenM Tower of London
hotels.highlight: Ultra-modern, compact boutique hotel with floor-to-ceiling city views steps from the Tower of London.

hotels.name: Generator London
hotels.highlight: Award-winning design hostel near King's Cross with a cocktail bar, cinema, and free walking tours.

spots.name: Tower of London
spots.highlight: 1,000-year-old fortress, home to the Crown Jewels, ravens that must never leave (or the kingdom falls), and grim medieval history.

spots.name: British Museum
spots.highlight: The world's largest free museum — the Rosetta Stone, Elgin Marbles, Egyptian mummies, and 8 million artefacts.

spots.name: Hyde Park & Kensington Gardens
spots.highlight: London's green lung — Speaker's Corner, the Serpentine lake, Princess Diana Memorial, and Kensington Palace.

spots.name: Camden Market
spots.highlight: London's most eclectic market district — vintage clothes, street art, global street food, and live alternative music.

spots.name: Tate Modern & Thames Southbank
spots.highlight: Former power station now housing the world's greatest modern art museum — free entry and a Turbine Hall the size of an aircraft carrier.

schedule.activity: Join a Yeoman Warder (Beefeater) tour. See the Crown Jewels and walk across the glass floor of Tower Bridge.
Eat your way through London's most celebrated food market — Neal's Yard cheese, Monmouth coffee, hot salt beef bagels.
Explore Tate Modern's Turbine Hall and rotating exhibitions. Walk the Thames Southbank to the Millennium Bridge.
Spend the morning in the Great Court. See the Rosetta Stone, Sutton Hoo helmet, and Lewis Chessmen.
schedule.transport: Tube to Holborn or Tottenham Court Rd

schedule.activity: Watch street performers in the piazza. Walk West End theatreland. Lunch at Rules, London's oldest restaurant (1798).
Stroll through Kensington Gardens. Walk to the colourful Notting Hill Gate, Portobello Road, and pastel-painted townhouses.
See Big Ben (Elizabeth Tower), Westminster Abbey, and watch the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace.
Explore Camden's anarchic market — vinyl records, vintage combat jackets, and incredible street food from every continent.
Walk Brick Lane and Shoreditch for the world's greatest concentration of street art, vintage markets, and curry houses.

amsterdam.description: The Venice of the North — a city of 165 canals, 1,500 bridges, the world's most bicycle-friendly streets, and more museums per square kilometre than anywhere on earth.

overview.tips: Book the Anne Frank House months in advance — it sells out. Rent a bike, not a taxi. Visit Keukenhof in April-May for tulip fields. The Jordaan neighbourhood is the most beautiful area.

hotels.name: Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam
hotels.highlight: Six interconnected 17th-century canal palaces converted into a museum-quality luxury hotel on the Golden Bend.

hotels.name: Hotel V Nesplein
hotels.highlight: Stylish boutique hotel on a characterful alley in the historic center with a canal-view breakfast room.

hotels.name: Stayokay Amsterdam Vondelpark
hotels.highlight: Unique hostel inside the Vondelpark forest with garden terraces, bar and bike rental.

spots.name: Anne Frank House
spots.highlight: The secret annex where Anne Frank and her family hid for 2 years — profoundly moving, entirely authentic.

spots.name: Rijksmuseum
spots.highlight: The Dutch national museum — Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's The Milkmaid, and 8,000 masterpieces of the Dutch Golden Age.

spots.name: Van Gogh Museum
spots.highlight: The world's largest collection of Van Gogh works — 200 paintings including The Bedroom and Sunflowers in chronological journey.

spots.name: Jordaan Neighbourhood & Canal Ring
spots.highlight: The most charming district in Europe — narrow canal-side streets of gabled houses, independent boutiques, and brown cafes (bruine kroegen).

spots.name: Heineken Experience
spots.highlight: The original Heineken brewery transformed into an interactive brand experience with a free beer included at the end.

schedule.activity: Walk through the secret annex where Anne Frank wrote her diary. Pre-book your time slot — opens at 9am.
Cycle the Prinsengracht, Keizersgracht, and Herengracht canals. Stop at a brown cafe for broodjes and jenever (gin).
Join an evening canal cruise when the canal house lights reflect in the water — the most romantic 75 minutes in Amsterdam.
Book the first morning slot. See Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's Milkmaid, and the medieval collection.
Walk chronologically through Van Gogh's life from dark Dutch winters to the blazing yellows of Provence.
Tour the Heineken brewery, then explore the diverse De Pijp neighbourhood for Indonesian rijsttafel dinner.
Take the bus to the world's largest flower garden (April-May only, 800 acres of tulips). Or Vondelpark alternative year-round.
Visit the dramatic green-hulled NEMO building on the Amsterdam harbour roof terrace — panoramic city view for free.

istanbul.description: The City on Two Continents — a 3,000-year-old city straddling Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus Strait, where Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman domes, and the world's best baklava share every neighbourhood.

overview.tips: Get an Istanbulkart for public transport. Bargain at the Grand Bazaar (start at 40% of asking price). Take the ferry across the Bosphorus — cheapest and best view in the city. Avoid large-denomination notes when haggling.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet
hotels.highlight: A converted 19th-century prison steps from the Hagia Sophia — courtyard garden and Ottoman luxury.

hotels.name: Hotel Ibrahim Pasha
hotels.highlight: Elegant boutique hotel with a rooftop terrace directly facing the Blue Mosque — unbeatable location.

hotels.name: Cheers Hostel Istanbul
hotels.highlight: Beloved rooftop-terrace hostel with Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia views — backpacker institution.

spots.name: Hagia Sophia
spots.highlight: The most awe-inspiring building in the world — a 6th-century Byzantine cathedral converted to mosque in 1453, now a mosque again with mosaics restored.

spots.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmet Camii)
spots.highlight: The only mosque in the world with six minarets — its interior dazzles with 20,000 hand-painted İznik blue tiles.

spots.name: Topkapi Palace
spots.highlight: The 600-year imperial palace of the Ottoman sultans — treasure house of 86-carat Spoonmaker's Diamond, emerald dagger, and the Prophet's relics.

spots.name: Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı)
spots.highlight: The world's oldest covered market (1461) — 4,000 shops across 61 streets selling carpets, spices, gold, lamps, and Turkish delight.

spots.name: Bosphorus Cruise
spots.highlight: A 2-hour ferry ride through the Bosphorus Strait separating Europe from Asia — yali mansions, military fortresses, and two continents at once.

schedule.activity: Visit first thing before crowds. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and the mingling of Christian and Islamic iconography.
Walk across to the Blue Mosque (closed during prayer times). See the ancient Egyptian obelisk in the Hippodrome square.
Explore the treasury (with the Spoonmaker's Diamond), harem, and the Prophet's Cloak relics in the sacred pavilion.
Spend 2 hours negotiating in the world's oldest covered mall — buy hand-painted İznik ceramics, evil eye beads, and Turkish carpets.
Fill a bag with saffron, rose petals, Turkish delight, and dried fruit from the 17th-century bazaar.
Take the public ferry from Eminönü to Sarıyer and back — a 2-hour return cruise through the Bosphorus strait.
Climb the medieval Galata Tower for a 360° panorama over the Golden Horn. Explore the hip Karaköy neighbourhood below.
Wander the colourful Greek-Jewish-Ottoman neighbourhood of Balat with its pastel houses, antique shops, and bohemian cafes.
Walk the 1.4km pedestrian Istiklal Caddesi. Drink at a meyhane (traditional tavern), listen to live fasıl music.

prague.description: The City of a Hundred Spires — a perfectly preserved medieval fairy-tale city where Gothic towers, Baroque palaces, and Art Nouveau cafes line cobblestone streets on the Vltava River.

overview.tips: The Old Town is very walkable — no need for taxis in the center. Buy a 3-day metro pass. Trdelník (the spiral chimney cake) is a tourist trap — skip it. Avoid the touristy Czech food traps on Old Town Square.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Prague
hotels.highlight: Palatial riverside hotel with a direct Charles Bridge view from the terrace and Baroque-era stone vaults.

hotels.name: Hotel Maximilian
hotels.highlight: Stylish Art Nouveau-inspired boutique hotel in the Old Town with a delightful reading room and courtyard.

hotels.name: Czech Inn Hostel
hotels.highlight: Multiple Design Hostel of the Year awards — chic design, heated pool, sauna, and craft beer bar.

spots.name: Charles Bridge
spots.highlight: A 650-year-old Gothic bridge of 30 baroque saint statues over the Vltava — at dawn before the crowds, it is magical.

spots.name: Prague Castle Complex
spots.highlight: The world's largest ancient castle complex — St. Vitus Cathedral, Golden Lane, and panoramic city views.

spots.name: Old Town Square & Astronomical Clock
spots.highlight: Prague's medieval heart — every hour the 600-year-old Astronomical Clock performs a parade of apostle figures.

spots.name: Josefov Jewish Quarter
spots.highlight: The best-preserved Jewish ghetto in Europe — six synagogues, the Old Jewish Cemetery, and the harrowing Pinkas Synagogue memorial.

spots.name: Petřín Hill & Funicular
spots.highlight: A forested hill above the city with a miniature Eiffel Tower lookalike, mirror maze, and the best views of Prague's red rooftops.

schedule.activity: Walk the bridge before 7am when it is completely empty of tourists — just saints, mist, and the Vltava.
Walk up to the castle complex. Enter the cathedral — its Art Nouveau Mucha stained glass window is breathtaking.
Walk down from the castle through the Baroque gardens and Malá Strana neighbourhood — the most photogenic streets in Prague.
Watch the Astronomical Clock strike 10am. Explore the Romanesque and Gothic churches around the square.
Visit the six synagogues (especially Pinkas with 80,000 names) and the extraordinary stacked Old Jewish Cemetery.
Eat svíčková (beef with cream sauce) and drink Pilsner Urquell in a traditional pivnice (beer hall) in Žižkov.
Take the funicular up Petřín Hill. Visit the miniature Eiffel Tower lookout, Strahov Monastery, and mirror maze.
Walk the boulevard of Czech history — the 1968 and 1989 protest sites, Art Nouveau cafes, and the grand National Museum.

rio.description: The Marvellous City — where dramatic granite peaks drop straight into carnival-coloured favelas and Copacabana's golden crescent, and Christ watches over it all with open arms.

overview.tips: Never take your phone out on the beach at night. Use Uber not taxis. Book Sugarloaf and Christ the Redeemer at dawn for no queues. Santa Teresa is the best neighbourhood for art and nightlife.

hotels.name: Copacabana Palace
hotels.highlight: Legendary 1923 Art Deco beachfront hotel — the most iconic address on Copacabana Beach.

hotels.name: Hotel Santa Teresa
hotels.highlight: Boutique hilltop hotel in the artists' quarter with a pool, stunning city views, and a farm-to-table restaurant.

hotels.name: Mambembe Hostel Lapa
hotels.highlight: Social hostel in Rio's legendary Lapa nightlife district with a rooftop and samba lessons.

spots.name: Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor)
spots.highlight: The outstretched Art Deco statue (38m) on Corcovado Peak — one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

spots.name: Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar)
spots.highlight: Twin cable-car ascent to the iconic granite peak — panoramic views of Rio's harbours, beaches, and mountains.

spots.name: Copacabana Beach
spots.highlight: The world's most famous urban beach — 4km of golden sand, mosaic promenade, beach volleyball, and caipirinhas.

spots.name: Ipanema Beach & Sunset
spots.highlight: Rio's sophisticated beach for locals — the sunset from Arpoador Rock at the end of Ipanema is mythic.

spots.name: Lapa Arches & Neighbourhood
spots.highlight: The 18th-century Roman aqueduct arches now support a tram — below them, Rio's most authentic samba bars pulse every Friday.

schedule.activity: Book the first cable car or train up Corcovado. At sunrise the city below is bathed in gold — the most moving view in Rio.
schedule.transport: Van from Santa Teresa or Cosme Velho

schedule.activity: Explore the bohemian hillside neighbourhood by tram. Visit the MAST telescope museum and local art galleries.
Walk the Lapa aqueduct arches at night, drink caipirinhas from street vendors, and dance samba in open-air bars.
Take the two-stage cable car to Pão de Açúcar. See Guanabara Bay, Rio's airport, and Copacabana from above.
Stroll the mosaic promenade, rent a beach chair, eat açaí, and watch beach volleyball. Perfect people-watching.
Join the crowd at Arpoador Rock for the most spectacular beach sunset in Rio. The crowd applauds when the sun disappears.
Hike in the world's largest urban rainforest. See waterfalls, marmosets, and toucans just 20 minutes from downtown.
Tour the hallowed temple of world football — step onto the pitch where Pelé and Zico played, and the World Cup was decided.
Eat feijoada and dance forró and samba at the legendary three-floor antique warehouse bar in Lapa.

cusco.description: The Navel of the World — the ancient Inca capital and gateway to Machu Picchu, the lost city in the clouds, set among cloud-forest-draped Andean peaks at 3,400m.

overview.tips: Acclimatize 1-2 days in Cusco before Machu Picchu (altitude 3,400m). Book the Huayna Picchu mountain hike 3 months in advance — only 400 tickets per day. Coca tea helps altitude sickness.

hotels.name: Inkaterra Machu Picchu Pueblo Hotel
hotels.highlight: Luxury cloud-forest village resort with private cloud forest trails, orchid garden, and Andean spa.

hotels.name: Palacio del Inka Luxury Collection
hotels.highlight: 500-year-old palace built over the Inca Qorikancha sun temple — the most historically significant hotel in Peru.

hotels.name: Loki Hostel Cusco
hotels.highlight: Legendary backpacker hostel in a converted colonial mansion with a rooftop bar and daily Inca Trail trips.

spots.name: Machu Picchu
spots.highlight: The most extraordinary archaeological site on earth — an entire Inca citadel hidden in the clouds, never found by the Spanish.

spots.name: Huayna Picchu Peak
spots.highlight: The dramatic steep peak towering over Machu Picchu — the view looking down on the citadel from above is unforgettable.

spots.name: Sacred Valley of the Incas
spots.highlight: The Urubamba Valley between Cusco and Machu Picchu — terraced Inca farms, weaving villages, and snow-capped Andean backdrop.

spots.name: Pisac Inca Ruins & Market
spots.highlight: Dramatic hilltop Inca fortress with terraced farms, combined with the Sacred Valley's best indigenous artisan market below.

spots.name: Ollantaytambo Fortress
spots.highlight: The only Inca town still inhabited on its original plan — a 15th-century fortress-temple with giant carved stone sun blocks.

schedule.activity: Acclimatize in Cusco's stunning colonial Plaza de Armas. Drink coca tea at a café. Visit the Catedral and Qorikancha Inca temple.
Walk or taxi up to the massive Inca fortress walls just above Cusco — zigzag limestone blocks weighing 360 tonnes, fitted without mortar.
Explore the artisan quarter of San Blas. Dine on alpaca steak and quinoa soup in a colonial courtyard restaurant.
Guided tour through the Sacred Valley — Pisac market, Inca terraces, salt pans at Maras, and the circular Moray ruins.
Train from Cusco to Aguas Calientes. Bus up to the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) first, then descend into the full citadel. Book Huayna Picchu if available.
